about.title: About Articulorium
about.intro: Articulorium is a W3C Linked Data Platform with Fedora Commons compatible extensions: versions (Memento), fixity checks and search, on an OCFL storage layer.

feature.browse: browse containers and resources, with their properties and children;
feature.create: create basic, direct and indirect containers and upload binaries;
feature.edit: edit properties with SPARQL Update, replace and download binary content;
feature.versions: create, list and view versions, and check the fixity of binaries;
feature.delete: delete resources and search the repository.

topology.intro: A topology describes the PCDM structure of a kind of digital object: its levels (collections and objects), their metadata fields, their kinds of files and how many children each level has. Build one in any container from its Topology panel, or in a collection from the Communities page.

panel.buildIntro: Create the PCDM structure of a book, newspaper, journal, postcards or a custom topology in this container.
panel.serviceUnavailable: The topology service is not available.

harvest.heading: Harvest
harvest.intro: Harvesting copies records from other repositories (OAI-PMH data providers, DSpace, Fedora and VIVO) into the platform. An incremental harvest reads what changed since the last complete harvest; a full harvest reads every record again.
harvest.readOnly: You can follow harvests here. Starting and cancelling them needs write access to the harvested records.
harvest.none: No harvest sources are configured. Operators add them to the harvest service’s settings (articulorium.harvest.sources).
harvest.never: Not harvested since the harvest service started.

why.permission: Starting harvests needs write access to the harvested records.
why.disabled: This source is disabled in the harvest service’s settings.
why.running: A harvest of this source is running.
why.notIncremental: This source cannot list only what changed: every harvest of it is a full harvest.

confirmFull.title: Start a full harvest?
confirmFull.message: A full harvest reads every record of {{source}} again and replaces their copies. It can take a long time, and it does not remove copies of records the source no longer lists.

confirmCancel.title: Cancel the harvest?
confirmCancel.message: The harvest of {{source}} stops after the record in progress. Records already stored stay; the checkpoint does not move, so the next incremental harvest reads the same changes again.

running.stopping: Stopping after the record in progress…

checkpoint.moved: Checkpoint saved: the next incremental harvest reads changes since {{time}}.
checkpoint.kept: Checkpoint not moved: the next incremental harvest reads the same changes again.
